One should not say so … [as before] … Is all knowledge the analytical knowledges?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is all wisdom analytical knowledge (paṭisambhidā)?
One should not say so …pe…
Is all wisdom analytical knowledge? Yes.
For one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, there is wisdom; is that wisdom analytical knowledge?
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … the water-kasiṇa … the fire-kasiṇa … [and so on].
the air kasiṇa …pe… the blue kasiṇa …pe… the yellow kasiṇa …pe…
the red kasiṇa … the white kasiṇa … the base of infinite space … and so forth.
For one who has attained the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the base of nothingness …pe… the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe…
To one giving a gift …pe… to one giving a robe …pe… to one giving almsfood …pe…
When one gives lodging, or when one gives medicinal requisites for the sick, there is wisdom; is that wisdom the analytical knowledge (*paṭisambhidā*)?
One should not say so... [and so on].
Is it not to be said that “all knowledge is analytical insight”?
Yes, it is.
Is there supramundane wisdom that is not analytical knowledge?
One must not say so...
[and so on] ...therefore, all knowledge is analytical knowledge.
The Discourse on the Analytical Knowledges is finished.
